steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degree F oven (175 degree C).
Place crushed ramen noodles and cashew pieces on a baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown.
Combine coleslaw, green onions, ramen noodles, and cashews in a large bowl.
Whisk sugar, oil, vinegar and soy sauce together in a bowl. Pour vinaigrette over coleslaw mixture; toss and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chinese Cabbage Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Chinese cabbage salad recipe combines golden toasted ramen noodles, cashews, shredded cabbage, and green onions with a soy sauce vinaigrette.
raw_recipe.name: Chinese Cabbage Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degree F oven (175 degree C).
Place crushed ramen noodles and cashew pieces on a baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown.
Combine coleslaw, green onions, ramen noodles, and cashews in a large bowl.
Whisk sugar, oil, vinegar and soy sauce together in a bowl. Pour vinaigrette over coleslaw mixture; toss and serve.

review.reviewBody: WOW!! This salad definitley deserves 5 stars. The dressing is out of this world. I did add 1 tablespoon of sesame oil and 1 tablespoon of sesame seeds to the dressing and decreased the amount of oil to 1/3 cup. I put the dressing in a glass jar and shook it well. I let it sit for about 10 minutes to let the flavors develop. I used sliced almonds instead of cashews and toasted the ramen noodles in a skillet before sprinkling them on top. I bet rotisserie chicken tossed in would be a great addition too. Do not add the dressing unitl right before your ready to serve, otherwise it will become soggy. I give this salad my highest recommendation.

I made this salad for a gathering of about 40 people and everyone raved. It took about an hour to prepare the way I did it. I thinly sliced 2 large heads of green cabbage. I used 6 bunches of green onions. I chopped a 15 oz. container of whole almonds (because I had them in the house) and toasted them in melted butter in a large stainless fry pan. Put them in a large bowl then melted some more butter in the same pan and stirred in 5 packages of crushed ramen noodles with the chicken flavor packets sprinkled over them, and cooked until toasted. Tossed the noodles and almonds together, and turned them out over the cabbage and green onions that I had put into a large roasting pan. I tripled the dressing ingredients, using rice vinegar instead of cider vinegar, and superfine sugar. I made the dressing first, before I started preparing everything else, so that the sugar would dissolve and the flavors blend. Poured the dressing over everything and tossed it a bit and it was fabulous!

Okay... can't rate it a 5 because I did change quite a few things... I was looking for a good dinner salad, but didn't have my 'normal' recipe handy. I didn't have Soy sauce and subbed Worcestershire. Sautéed the cashews, Ramen noodles, some sesame seeds and seasoning from the noodles in a bit of sesame oil... Subbed Rice Wine vinegar for the cider vinegar and added a touch of sesame oil to the dressing... Added a can of chicken since I was looking for an entrée salad, but will probably use fresh grilled next time. Used Angel Hair slaw mix (2 pkgs) and mixed that with the green onion and chicken in a large bowl. Mixed the dressing ingredients in a jar and let sit for 15 minutes. When ready to sit down stirred the dressing into the greens and chicken, but withheld the 'crunchies'. Dished up servings and then let folks shake on the amount of crunchies to their taste. It was all terrific and my husband actually liked it better than my 'regular' recipe. Keeping the crunchies in a separate container made it easy to keep those dry for the leftovers, but mixing all of the dressing into the greens allowed the flavors to really come through! It was almost better the 2nd time! Sorry for the long review... I wanted to save my notes while I still remembered them all!!!

This is very good. I followed one reviewer's suggestion to pan toast the cashews and noodles after spraying with some Pam and sprinkling on the seasoning packet. This is very good advice. I also substituted rice vinegar for the cider. Otherwise I followed the recipe. I have to agree with others that there is too much oil. It leaves an oily feeling on the lips which is not pleasant. As we tend to like sour, next time I will add a bit more vinegar as well as cutting the oil. Adding in a sprinkling of sesame seeds would probably be a nice addition as well. I think I would suggest adding the dressing to the cole slaw about 1/2 hour before serving to allow it to take in some of the flavors and adding the crunchy elements right before serving. I think with those tweaks this will be a repeat recipe for us!

Excellent (with modifications) - 5 STARS!

I made this recipe for Christmas dinner....NO leftovers! I will definitely make again! It's a keeper :)
Modifications: 
Left out the cashews
2 ramen noodle packets instead of 1
Sauteed the noodles in a skillet with a little butter instead of using the oven
Added seasoning packet to dressing mixture, and simmered the dressing to emulsify it

We love it!.. My additions are 1/2 tsp. sesame oil in the dressing and also some sesame seeds on the salad looks pretty! For a main dish I add cooked/breaded/chopped chicken (Tyson), mandarin oranges and a little chopped Italian parsley when I have it. So yummy! Be sure you whisk enough so it will emulsify before pouring on.; my preference is to pour over about 15 min before because the ramen can be pretty crunchy.. :)

The dressing is wonderful, but I like it a little more acetic (vinegar). Unlike some reviewers, I think the slaw mixture should be allowed to marinate with the dressing for about an hour then adding the crunchy ingredients right before serving. The cabbage needs time to absorb some of the flavors. I pan toasted the noodles, cashews and added some sesame seeds, used some sesame oil in the dressing. The leftovers make a fantastic stir fry... just add an egg and some meat.

Added some cilantro, and used napa cabbage, carrot, and a couple of radishes instead of a bagged mix. I also cut the sugar and oil to a little more than half of what the recipe called for. With those changes, excellent.

I've been making a slightly different version of this salad for years and decided to adopt some of the differences this recipe calls for. I toasted the ramen noodles, which I hadn't done before, a definite improvement,,along with chopped almonds instead of the cashews and also added sesame seeds which we all like. I cut back on the sugar to 3 Tablespoons which is plenty. I added about a tablespoon of sesame oil for part of the oil and added
Lower sodium soy sauce which my original recipe didn't call for. I brought the new and improved version to a family gathering and it was well liked by all. I like changing things up and will make this new version the next time I'm hungry for Chinese cabbage salad.

I made this with a bit less oil as others suggested, and added cilantro (but still rating 5 because I feel my changes did not alter the original taste enough to make the that big of a difference, I feel these are a matter of preference) and this was delicious! I added in some chicken to make it more filling. I just browned the chicken and then poured some of the dressing to caramelize in with it. Next time I think the only thing I'll change is using something other than Ramen, because the texture was not quite crunchy enough for my taste.. I think I will try the crunchy wonton strips you can buy at the store next time.

Made this with way less sugar!... I used only 2 tbls of sugar to be exact. Probably could have gotten away with just one tbls. Added a tsp of sesame oil. About a 1/4-1/2 cup of chopped cilantro, subed cider vinegar for seasoned rice vinegar, added a tsp of fresh grated ginger, and two med shredded carrots. Was great, the whole family loved it! We topped it with sliced and grilled pork chops marinated with Asian ingredients.
I would give it 5 stars, but this recipe uses far too much oil. Instead, I used 1/4 cup oil along with a teaspoon of sesame oil.
This turned out very well! The only changes that I made were using unsalted peanuts instead of cashews and that I shredded the cabbage rather than using a bag already shredded. Great recipe!!

My daughter and I are doing a weekly cook off of different ethnic foods. 
i made this it was simple and quick. 5 stars from me it was the top pick this week!!!
Added chicken for protein. It was great.

Delicious salad! I added a small bunch cilantro, seeded and diced cucumber, and diced radishes for extra crunch. I added a teaspoon of sesame oil to the dressing. Instead of coleslaw I chopped up a head of cabbage. I served the salad with rotisserie chicken on top. I also doubled the ramen and cashews because that’s my favorite part! Yum. Thanks for the recipe!!
Excellent! Before changing it all around try following the recipe as written, it is easy to prepare, and delicious...you will not be disappointed! Suck
Sooooo good! Reminded me of a salad my mom used to make for family potlucks. Added 2 T. Sesame oil and seeds and turned out great, thank you for a great recipe.
